changes: Notes expanded: the right-to-left chronogram reading, the unclear words giridāyāṃ / gauḍamadhya-, and the Gauḍa (amānta) month reckoning

date.as_written: navanavatihutāśaiś cihnite lakṣmaṇābde gatavati giridāyāṃ gauḍamadhyāśvinasya (?) | iha timiradaśamyām

notes: The chronogram is navanavati (99) plus hutāśa (3 fires). Read right to left, it gives LS 399, which matches the catalogue. LS 399 + 1119 gives about 1518 CE. 'gatavati' means the year had elapsed. 'timiradaśamī' means the dark-fortnight 10th. 'gauḍamadhyāśvina' (marked ? by the cataloguer) seems to mean Āśvina by the Gauḍa reckoning, which is probably amānta. 'giridāyāṃ' is unclear. It may be corrupt, or it may be a place name in the locative, but it is not recorded as the place of copying.
